_comment: Regression set for lib/jev/questions.ts. Every expectation here was
hand-adjudicated against the participant record and the caseworker's
messages from two real runs (wrun_01M37CZX, wrun_01M37HH5), not copied
from what Jev happened to answer. Where Jev and the adjudication
disagreed, the adjudication wins and the case documents a known gap.
special_needs false, four phone numbers, address in WILDOMAR CA 92595.

Two axes, independent: `expectVerdict` judges the VALUE against the record and the caseworker's messages; `expectSourceAccurate`/`expectSensitive` judge the agent's own LABEL. A value that was badly inferred but honestly labelled `inferred` is verdict=unsupported AND sourceAccurate=high.
caseworkerMessages: Fill out IHSS at https://riversideihss.org/IntakeApp for the participant below. This JSON is all the participant data available - there is no database to look up.

Answers for IHSS Application (SOC 295) - Riverside County:
- Social Security Number: 123224444
- Telephone (which number to list): 555-555-5555
- Briefly describe your health history: disabled
- Please check any of the following that apply: Unable to perform some activities of daily living (bathing, feeding, dressing, walking, etc.)

summary.why: Verbatim from participant.name.first, labelled record. Control case: both axes should be confidently right.
Record says 'California'; 'CA' is the same value in the form's format. Reformatting must not read as invention.

NEGATIVE CONTROL for the sourceAccurate axis. The value is in the record, so the verdict is grounded, but the caseworker never said it - the label is wrong and sourceAccurate must drop. Without this case a scorer cannot tell a calibrated sourceAccurate from a constant one.
Only in caseworker message 2, never in the record.

KNOWN GAP. The value is in BOTH contact_information.phones.home and message 2. The record holds four numbers, so the caseworker's answer is what selects this one - caseworker_supplied should win. Run wrun_01M37HH5 returned grounded 0.62 / caseworker_supplied 0.30, so the disjointness clause in SUMMARY_VERDICTS is not deciding this.

summary.field: Are you applying to receive IHSS for yourself?
summary.why: The task names the participant as the applicant and the record holds one person. Unanswerable from the record alone - this is the case that proves caseworker_messages reached Jev. Was unsupported 0.78 before P1, grounded 0.66 after.

KNOWN GAP. marital_status 'Single parent household' implies the participant does not live alone. Run wrun_01M37CZX said grounded; after the stricter default-answer clause wrun_01M37HH5 said unsupported 0.63. A defensible inference is being read as invention. NOTE: this case sits on the decision boundary and has been observed BOTH ways on identical input — unsupported 0.63 in run wrun_01M37HH5, grounded 0.54 in a later direct call. It is the clearest evidence that single-run verdict comparisons are unsafe, and the reason this suite repeats each case (JEV_EVAL_REPEATS, default 3).

summary.field: Is the application for a minor adopted child?
summary.why: KNOWN GAP. DOB 2000-01-02 makes the applicant an adult, and age-from-DOB is an accepted inference in evals/online/scorers/summary-attribution.ts. Jev's state carries no reference date, so it cannot compute age at all. Went 0.88 unsupported -> 0.58 unsupported / 0.40 grounded after P1: moving, not fixed.

summary.field: Check your type of living arrangement
summary.why: Nothing in the record establishes the IHSS living-arrangement category. Held at unsupported 0.83 / 0.88 across both runs - the case that proves the wording has not become too permissive. The `source` label 'inferred' is ACCURATE here even though the inference itself is unsupported: `verdict` judges the value, `sourceAccurate` judges the label, and the two are independent. Expecting low here was an error in the first draft of this set — observed 0.53-0.74.

summary.field: Please check any of the following that apply
summary.why: An unexamined default submitted as an answer. Distinct from the caseworker-answered version of the same field in run wrun_01M37HH5. The `source` label 'inferred' is ACCURATE here even though the inference itself is unsupported: `verdict` judges the value, `sourceAccurate` judges the label, and the two are independent. Expecting low here was an error in the first draft of this set — observed 0.53-0.74.

BORDERLINE by adjudication. special_needs false is a generic flag, not a statement about a specific IHSS eligibility category. Firmed 0.52 -> 0.70 after the default-answer clause. Kept so that if policy later decides the flag IS sufficient, this case flips deliberately rather than silently. The `source` label 'inferred' is ACCURATE here even though the inference itself is unsupported: `verdict` judges the value, `sourceAccurate` judges the label, and the two are independent. Expecting low here was an error in the first draft of this set — observed 0.53-0.74.

Same as weak-flag-blind. Firmed 0.38 -> 0.75. Synthetic. The only exercise of the contradicts_record verdict - no real run produced one, so without this case that branch is untested.

gap.why: Not in the record, and sensitive - drove sensitive 0.95 in both runs.
Medical detail, not in the record. sensitive 0.93 observed.

gap.field: Do you have anyone available to provide assistance at home?
gap.why: Not in the record but not sensitive. sensitive 0.13 observed - the case that proves the sensitive axis discriminates rather than firing on everything.
NEGATIVE CONTROL. The record holds date_of_birth, so asking the caseworker for it wastes their turn. No real run produced a present_in_record verdict, so this branch is otherwise untested.

Not stated but follows from date_of_birth - the verdict GAP_VERDICTS names explicitly. Pairs with age-derived-adult above: if Jev cannot do age-from-DOB for want of a reference date, both fail together and the cause is one gap, not two.
